newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power slips, Southwest higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power slips, Southwest higher.

text.p: Spot power prices in the US Northwest slipped further today amid continued surplus supplies, while Southwest prices ticked up in reaction to a short-term coal plant outage in the Rocky Mountains.
Daily cash prices at Palo Verde in Arizona were last quoted $24.75-25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $22.00-23.00 early Monday.

Traders said the unplanned outage on Saturday of Basin Electric Power Cooperative's Laramie River coal-fired generating unit 3 spilled over into the Southwest when some transmissions into the Four Corners region were affected.
But the 550-MW unit was expected to return to service on Wednesday and traders said they expect the price boost to be short-lived.
Offers at Four Corners were seen Tuesday at $24.00-25.00.
In the Northwest, however, lower price offers from the Bonneville Power Administration, along with cooler temperatures and forecasts for above-normal rainfall, pushed cash prices downward.
Bonneville lowered its standing offer for next-day power during peak-demand hours by $1.00 to $17.00 per MWh.
Daily prices at the California-Oregon border were last assessed near $16.00, down from $17.00-18.00 on Monday.
October prices for both COB and Palo Verde were little changed from Monday at $16.00-16.50 and $16.30-16.60, respectively.
